title: 1970 Mount Everest disaster
text:
On 5 April 1970, an avalanche killed six Nepalese Sherpa porters on the Khumbu Icefall of Mount Everest.  The porters were assisting the Japanese Everest Skiing Expedition 1970 climbing expedition.  Four days later Sherpa Kyak Tsering, a porter on a different Japanese Mt. Everest expedition, was killed by ice falling from a serac. Later, Yūichirō Miura, the focus of the film expedition, became the first person to ski down Everest.
The icefall, which lies between Base Camp and Camp I, has been the site of numerous fatalities, including those in the 2014 Mount Everest ice avalanche.  The six 1970 victims were Mima Norbu, Nima Dorje, Tshering Tarkey, Pasang, Kunga Norbu, and Kami Tshering.
